title: Field protocol v1 checkpoint event (Field to core)
description: A Field's offer of a resume point. The Field proposes; core commits. Core commits the cursor only after every record with a sequence number at or below 'covers_record_seq_through' has reached durable current state, artifacts first, and the store's durability barrier has returned. A checkpoint carries no credential and no source payload. In snapshot mode it also carries the completeness claim that is the only thing which can authorize removal by proven absence.

covers_record_seq_through.description: Sequence number of the last record this cursor accounts for. Must be less than this checkpoint's own seq, and greater than or equal to the previous checkpoint's value in the same run. Zero means no records are covered at all -- the cursor advances without any record in between, which a Field may emit when it has proven that a page contained nothing new. Equal to the previous checkpoint's value means repeated coverage of an already-covered range: legal, and a no-op that accounts for zero new records. Eligibility for commit means every accepted *record* with seq at or below this value is durable, not that every seq in that range is durable: seq is shared by records, checkpoints, and diagnostics, so a diagnostic's or another checkpoint's seq falling inside the range proves nothing about it. A naive implementation that builds a '(previous + 1)..=covers' range to count covered records must special-case 'covers' not having advanced past 'previous', because ranging a sorted set backwards panics rather than yielding an empty range.

records_covered.description: Count of record events this checkpoint accounts for since the previous checkpoint. Core cross-checks it against what it actually received and fails the run as 'protocol.coverage_mismatch' on disagreement -- not 'protocol.unexpected_order', which is reserved for a frame arriving somewhere the protocol does not allow it at all.

snapshot.description: Present only in a snapshot-mode run. 'complete' is the Field's explicit claim that it enumerated the whole declared scope. Anything else, including a partial claim, a windowed run, an error diagnostic anywhere in the run, cancellation, a deadline, or a non-zero exit, leaves absence meaningless: core removes nothing. When a claim is invalid for more than one reason at once, core reports 'snapshot.completeness_contradicted' before 'snapshot.scope_widened': whether the run and manifest even admit a completeness claim at all is checked first, and only a claim that clears that bar is then checked against the requested scope.

scope.description: The scope this claim covers. Must equal the request's snapshot_scope; a wider claim is rejected.

window.description: The portion of a requested window this checkpoint accounts for. A window is bounded evidence and never authorizes deletion.

final.description: The Field's declaration that this is the last checkpoint of the run and it intends to exit normally. A run whose process exits non-zero is never treated as complete regardless of this flag.
